polymarket.rules_excerpt: This market will resolve to "Yes" if the named individual wins and accepts the 2028 nomination of the Democratic Party for U.S. president. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No". The resolution source for this market will be a consensus of official Democratic Party sources. Any replacement of the democratic nominee before election day will not change the resolution of the market.

review.note: Draft, not confirmed. Both pay on Pritzker winning and accepting the 2028 Democratic nomination, in nearly the same words. review.note: Draft, not confirmed. Both venues require explicit, formal recognition of Somaliland as a sovereign state before 2027-01-01 and both exclude mere acknowledgment, consulates or liaison offices. Polymarket names official US government information as primary source with credible reporting as fallback; Kalshi lists qualifying acts (embassy, ambassador, State Department country list, treaty). This market pertains to the outcome of the next French presidential election, regardless of whether it follows the scheduled end of the current term or is held earlier. The President of France is elected via a two-round system; a candidate must secure over 50% of the vote to win outright in the first round. If no candidate achieves this, the top two contenders advance to a runoff. This market will resolve according to the candidate who wins this election. This market includes any potential second round. …

review.note: Draft, not confirmed. Both pay on Le Pen winning the next French presidential election including a second round. polymarket.question: Will Donald Trump win the 2028 US Presidential Election?
polymarket.rules_excerpt: The 2028 US Presidential Election is scheduled to take place on November 7, 2028. This market will resolve to the person who wins the 2028 US Presidential Election. The resolution source for this market is the Associated Press, Fox News, and NBC. This market will resolve once all three sources call the race for the same candidate. If all three sources haven't called the race for the same candidate by the inauguration date (January 20, 2029) this market will resolve based on who is inaugurated.

review.note: Kalshi pays on who is next inaugurated as President for the term beginning in 2029; Polymarket pays on who wins the election as called by AP, Fox News and NBC, and falls back to the inauguration only if the three do not agree. A candidate who wins the election and is not inaugurated (death, withdrawal, a disputed certification) pays YES on Polymarket and NO on Kalshi. A basket over this pair loses both legs instead of hedging.
